feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Stopping and Routing LLM Judge Panels
entry.summary:
A new role-conditioned allocation framework optimizes LLM judge panels by classifying candidate judges into roles to derive cost-effective stopping and routing policies from a small audit set.

Why it matters: It replaces ad-hoc or full-ensemble judge calls with an auditable, cost-efficient call plan that optimizes inference spending while maintaining evaluation accuracy.

entry.title: Projector Is All You Train
entry.summary:
Training only the projector in multimodal LLMs delivers strong performance on 3D tasks without needing to fine-tune the language backbone.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces MLLM training compute costs and speeds up throughput while fully preserving original language model capabilities.

entry.title: Forking Fast: Efficiently Estimating Uncertainty Dynamics in Text Generation
entry.summary:
Researchers developed a statistical model that smoothes low-sample rollout data to efficiently estimate uncertainty dynamics in LLM text generation at a fraction of the computational cost.

Why it matters: It enables researchers to analyze LLM reasoning chains and uncertainty dynamics far more efficiently without incurring the massive computational overhead of extensive sequence resampling.

entry.title: When Machines Speak: A Unified Generative Framework for Integrating Machine-Native Symbols into Pretrained Large Language Models
entry.summary:
UniLang expands pretrained LLM vocabulary and embedding spaces to autoregressively generate machine-native discrete symbols alongside natural-language tokens within a unified framework.

Why it matters: It enables LLMs to serve as a unified generative backbone for structured prediction and machine-native data without losing domain-specific structural information.

entry.title: Break It Down, Pass It On: Cross-Task Skill Transfer in LLM Agents
entry.summary:
A controlled study reveals that subtask-level and text-formatted skills transfer better in LLM agents than task-level and code-based skills, introducing a non-execution-based skill utility score to predict transfer success.

Why it matters: System designers can improve LLM agent memory reliability and diagnose skill quality before execution without running costly, multi-step task evaluations.

entry.title: Daedalus-150M: A Convolution-Attention Hybrid Designed for CPU Inference
entry.summary:
Daedalus-150M is a 4-bit CPU-optimized language model that replaces full attention with 2-timestep short convolutions in 12 of its 18 blocks, achieving faster decode speeds and higher benchmark scores.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that replacing attention with fixed-memory convolutions in most transformer layers significantly improves CPU inference speed and context scaling without sacrificing task quality.

entry.title: Optimal Skill Selection for LLM Agents with Provable Bicriteria Guarantees
entry.summary:
Best Prefix Selection (BPS) optimizes LLM agent skill retrieval under token budgets, achieving a provable bicriteria (1-1/e, 1) approximation guarantee.

Why it matters: It eliminates context window waste and performance degradation caused by independent semantic scoring and greedy skill packing in LLM agents.

entry.title: Interrupting the Loop: Periodic Subject Changes Raise Judged Surprise and Connection in Base Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers isolated a specific mechanism in base LLMs where injecting periodic subject interruptions combined with habituation significantly increases judged surprise and connection, though it fails to produce cohesive long-form documents.

Why it matters: Periodic subject interruption provides a simple method to boost local creative diversity in base LLMs, while highlighting critical flaws in window-based LLM evaluation protocols for long text generation.

entry.title: EXIMO: VLM Guided Exploration of VLA Policies
entry.summary:
EXIMO is a three-stage finetuning framework that uses a Vision-Language Model planner to guide Vision-Language-Action policies through exploration, imitation, and residual off-policy reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: EXIMO enables sample-efficient online adaptation of large VLA robot policies for new, long-horizon manipulation tasks without requiring extensive human teleoperation.

entry.title: Write Once, Run Everywhere: The Axon DSL for Shape-Safe and Framework-Agnostic LLM Architectures
entry.summary:
Axon is a strongly typed, Haskell-like domain-specific language that allows developers to write LLM architectures once and compile them directly to PyTorch, Triton, JAX, MLX, and vLLM.

Why it matters: Axon reduces the engineering burden of translating models across frameworks while delivering significant inference performance gains over standard reference implementations.

entry.title: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
entry.summary:
EnvHarness introduces a programmable layer of plug-in components that dynamically reshapes static environments around black-box agents without altering underlying logic or original verifiers.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need to manually engineer complex, domain-specific environment generation pipelines for LLM agent reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Listening Forward: Next Patch Embedding Prediction Enables Scalable Audio Learners
entry.summary:
NAPE introduces a minimalist self-supervised audio framework that uses a causal Transformer to predict the next log-mel spectrogram patch embedding using only causal masking and stop-gradients.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that simple autoregressive embedding prediction can match or exceed complex audio SSL pipelines, offering a unified pre-training strategy across modalities.

entry.title: Which Eviction Policy Should an LLM Cache Use? A Systematic Study Across Workloads, Capacities, and Encoders
entry.summary:
A systematic evaluation using the CLEVER protocol shows that LFU is the strongest simple eviction default for LLM semantic caches, as complex geometry-aware policies offer virtually no improvement over it.

Why it matters: System designers should default to LFU and focus on verifying answer validity and embedding-specific thresholds rather than implementing complex semantic eviction algorithms.

entry.title: Ask Self, Ask Others: Relation Is All You Need
entry.summary:
Relation is a token-mixing primitive that explicitly separates pairwise evidence into Self and Exchange relations before deriving information flow, outperforming Multi-Head Attention in validation loss.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that a relation-first approach to token mixing can improve language model validation loss while offering hardware-efficient execution variants comparable to FlashAttention.

entry.title: Feature Evolution and Migration during Vision Transformer Training
entry.summary:
A novel framework uses Sparse Autoencoders on CLS-token representations across training time and network depth to track feature evolution and feature migration in Vision Transformers.

Why it matters: This methodology provides a fine-grained feature-level tool to track, visualize, and understand internal model dynamics and layer-wise stabilization during ViT training.

entry.title: Reward-Guided Autoregressive Graph Generation for Efficient Multi-Agent Communication Topology Design
entry.summary:
RGA-Designer introduces an RLHF-inspired reward-guided autoregressive graph generation approach to design sparse multi-agent communication topologies that maintain reasoning accuracy while reducing token usage.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces LLM multi-agent operational costs by optimizing communication topology compactness without sacrificing task performance.

entry.title: Orthogonal JEPA: Factorized Predictive States for Latent World Models
entry.summary:
Orthogonal JEPA introduces orthogonal predictive factorization to latent world models, decomposing target states into distinct components predicted by dedicated branches from a shared context to prevent monolithic state redundancy.

Why it matters: By preventing dominant signals from overcrowding the latent space, Orthogonal JEPA improves predictive representation quality, long-horizon stability, and planning across complex, multi-scale dynamical systems.

entry.title: Scale-Aware Pretraining of Time Series Foundation Models via Multi-Patch Token Alignment and Hybrid Masking
entry.summary:
SATS introduces scale-aware pretraining for time series foundation models using multi-patch token alignment and a novel hybrid masking strategy.

Why it matters: It resolves representation fragmentation caused by varying temporal sampling frequencies, delivering state-of-the-art accuracy with significantly lower computational overhead.

entry.title: PolicyGuide: From Guarding One Action to Guiding the Whole Workflow for Policy-Compliant LLM Agents
entry.summary:
PolicyGuide compiles domain policies into workflow graphs and uses proactive verifiers at user-turn boundaries to provide step-specific remediation for policy-compliant LLM agents.

Why it matters: It shifts LLM safety from reactive, single-action checks to proactive, multi-step procedural guidance across complex customer-service workflows.

entry.title: MileGPO: Milestone Inference with Local Evidence for Graph-Based Policy Optimization of Long-Horizon LLM Agents
entry.summary:
MileGPO improves long-horizon LLM agent RL by inferring process-level milestones and traps from grouped on-policy rollouts using Reliability-Calibrated Shaping and Progress-Contrastive Calibration without extra environment interactions or auxiliary models.

Why it matters: MileGPO solves fine-grained credit assignment in sparse-reward environments without requiring auxiliary models or extra environment sampling.

entry.title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
ConceptGuard is a new benchmark for LLM unlearning that uses dual-use concepts to evaluate intent-sensitive contextual separation between harmful and benign uses of the same concept.

Why it matters: It establishes a realistic benchmark for verifying that LLMs can forget malicious applications of sensitive knowledge without destroying the model's useful, benign capabilities.

entry.title: FormalTCS: Benchmarking End-to-End Frontier Formal Theoretical Computer Science Research of Large Language Models
entry.summary:
FormalTCS is a benchmark of 175 Lean-formalized instances from recent STOC, FOCS, SODA, and COLT papers designed to evaluate LLMs on end-to-end theoretical computer science research.

Why it matters: The benchmark highlights that low autoformalization accuracy and poor research intuition are the primary factors preventing LLMs from autonomously conducting theoretical computer science research.

entry.title: When Text and Numbers Disagree: Evidence Arbitration in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
A new controlled synthetic benchmark reveals that open-weight LLMs rely on heuristic arbitration strategies, preferring specific modalities and recency over reliability cues when text, numbers, and forecasts conflict.

Why it matters: The heuristic evidence arbitration in current LLMs exposes a critical reliability failure mode for tool-augmented decision-making systems operating on heterogeneous data.

entry.title: SWE-bench Science: Can Coding Agents Resolve Engineering Tasks in Science?
entry.summary:
SWE-bench Science is a repository-level benchmark of 119 tasks across 98 GitHub repositories in 20 domains designed to evaluate coding agents on scientific software engineering.

Why it matters: It establishes a concrete framework for identifying how coding agents fail in scientific contexts, where software errors can directly compromise scientific evidence and conclusions.

entry.title: PersonalBench: Measuring the Authorship Gap in LLM Personalization
entry.summary:
PersonalBench evaluates inference-time LLM personalization, revealing that while methods create author-differentiated text, outputs remain dominated by the LLM's own authorship fingerprint and fail to reach human-level stylistic similarity.

Why it matters: Current inference-time personalization techniques only modulate LLM style superficially rather than bridging the underlying gap to true human authorship.

entry.title: Thinking in a Low-Resource Language: What SFT Builds, What RL Fixes, What Accuracy Cannot See
entry.summary:
Fine-tuning 3.6-4.0B active parameter MoE models shows accuracy benchmarks miss key updates, while SFT establishes target-language reasoning and RLVR resolves formatting, leakage, and instruction-following defects.

Why it matters: Evaluating reasoning models solely on accuracy masks crucial behavioural shifts and defects, requiring specialized length-independent dimensions and RLVR to build auditable, language-aligned LLMs.

entry.title: EXIMO: VLM Guided Exploration of VLA Policies
entry.summary:
EXIMO is an efficient algorithm for finetuning Vision-Language-Action (VLA) robot policies using a three-stage pipeline consisting of VLM-guided exploration, imitation learning, and residual off-policy reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: It reduces the need for costly human teleoperation data and overcomes RL sample inefficiency when adapting large VLA models to new long-horizon manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Towards Quantifying Benchmark Optimization in ASR Models
entry.summary:
A new methodology uses three behavioral probe families to show that top ASR models rely on benchmark-conditioned policies to output verbatim references even when audio is underdetermined, contradictory, or masked.

Why it matters: High public ASR benchmark scores may reflect benchmark-conditioned memorization rather than actual improvements in general-purpose speech recognition capabilities.

entry.title: TinyCast: Probabilistic Zero-Shot Forecasting with Computed Periodicity
entry.summary:
TinyCast is a 146,505-parameter attention-free zero-shot time-series forecaster that uses a zero-parameter spectral detector to compute periodicity rather than learning it.

Why it matters: It enables accurate, probabilistic zero-shot time-series forecasting on resource-constrained embedded devices without requiring online fine-tuning or large transformer architectures.

entry.title: PolicyGuide: From Guarding One Action to Guiding the Whole Workflow for Policy-Compliant LLM Agents
entry.summary:
PolicyGuide compiles domain policies into workflow graphs and uses proactive verifiers at user-turn boundaries to guide LLM agents through multi-step procedural compliance.

Why it matters: It shifts LLM agent safety from reactive, single-action guardrails to proactive, end-to-end procedural compliance across multi-turn customer service workflows.

entry.title: Chain-of-Experience for Continual LLM Improvement
entry.summary:
Chain-of-Experience (CoE) enables LLMs to continually improve at test time by accumulating experiential traces through iterative interactions with self-feedback or environmental feedback.

Why it matters: CoE offers a more token-efficient and cost-effective test-time adaptation strategy that allows LLMs to continuously self-improve without full retrain cycles.

entry.title: τ_0-VLA: a Hierarchical Robot Foundation Model with World-Model-Guided Test-Time Computation
entry.summary:
τ_0-VLA introduces a hierarchical robot foundation model that scales high-level subtask generation at inference time using world-model-guided search over candidate actions.

Why it matters: Allocating extra compute at test time allows VLA models to reason through complex choices, improving closed-loop execution and reliability on long-horizon robotic manipulation tasks.

entry.title: GOAG: Generative and Object-Agnostic Grasp Planner for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation
entry.summary:
GOAG is a generative, object-agnostic grasp planner that models a robot gripper's contact surface distribution to generate dexterous grasps without requiring object-specific training data.

Why it matters: By removing the need for object-specific training data, this approach solves key generalization barriers for multifingered robotic manipulators handling novel objects.

entry.title: CoToGrasp: Contact-Topology-Conditioned Dexterous Grasp Synthesis via Canonical Workspace Learning
entry.summary:
CoToGrasp is an object-agnostic generative framework that synthesizes functional, dexterous robot grasps conditioned strictly on contact topologies using a feature-based canonical workspace.

Why it matters: It enables robots to synthesize task-specific, functional dexterous grasps for novel objects without requiring costly object-annotated training data.

entry.title: Listening Forward: Next Patch Embedding Prediction Enables Scalable Audio Learners
entry.summary:
NAPE introduces a minimalist self-supervised framework for audio representation learning that trains a causal Transformer to predict the next log-mel spectrogram patch embedding using only causal masking and a stop-gradient.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that audio representation learning can achieve state-of-the-art results using a simple, scalable autoregressive prediction paradigm without complex pre-training recipes or specialized decoders.

entry.title: LLMs Get Smarter from Targeted Synthetic Multilingual Data
entry.summary:
The HOTFIXR framework identifies a student model's language-specific weaknesses and generates targeted synthetic multilingual training data to fix them without sacrificing overall model performance.

Why it matters: HOTFIXR enables developers to improve multilingual performance and cross-lingual reasoning in LLMs without degrading native expressivity or sacrificing general model capabilities.

entry.title: Evaluating Music Context Preservation: A Multi-facet Framework for Music Editing Systems
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced MuseCPEval, the first evaluation framework designed to assess Music Context Preservation across four categories of music facets in music editing systems.

Why it matters: MuseCPEval provides a standardized testbed and diagnostic tool to guide the development of more reliable music editing systems for film, broadcasting, and gaming.

entry.title: Bounded Agents: Delegation Security for Multi-Agent AI Systems
entry.summary:
The Agentic Principal Chain (APC) framework introduces a dynamic authorization architecture that tracks delegated authority, accumulates session state, and enforces six external security checks to mitigate multi-agent delegation risks.

Why it matters: By moving authorization out of the model and tracking cumulative session history, APC provides formal security guarantees against prompt injections and unauthorized sub-agent delegations.

entry.title: FlowEvo: Self-Evolving Agents through the Co-Evolution of Workflows and Executable Skills
entry.summary:
FlowEvo is a training-free framework that enables LLM agents to self-evolve by compiling successful inference-time workflows into a persistent library of executable skills.

Why it matters: It provides a token-efficient method for LLM agents to continuously learn and reuse complex task procedures without requiring model fine-tuning or offline skill compilation.

entry.title: SPK: Eliciting Structured Prior Knowledge for Interpretable Out-of-Distribution Detection in Real-Time Object Detection
entry.summary:
The Structured Prior Knowledge (SPK) framework explicitly elicits part-level semantic, geometric, and contextual latent priors from pretrained object detectors to achieve interpretable and state-of-the-art out-of-distribution (OoD) detection.

Why it matters: It enables safer real-time object detection by transforming black-box latent representations into an interpretable, 5D diagnostic space that reliably flags out-of-distribution hallucinations.

entry.title: What You Can't See Is What You Learn: Restricted Evidence Visibility Favors Compositional Generalization in Shared-Genome Language-Model Societies
entry.summary:
Restricting evidence visibility across four-cell language-model societies significantly improves compositional generalization, favoring reusable, value-indexed vector interfaces over globally visible architectures.

Why it matters: Enforcing information bottlenecks between modular language model components can reliably induce explicit, compositional, and counterfactually manipulable communication protocols without changing parameter counts or training data.

entry.title: Manifold Drift in Flow Preference Optimization: A Root Cause of Reward Hacking
entry.summary:
Researchers formalize manifold drift in flow matching preference optimization and propose ThermoDPO, a temperature-controlled objective that prevents terminal samples from drifting off the pretrained data support.

Why it matters: ThermoDPO mitigates reward hacking in continuous-time generative models by constraining preference-optimized updates to the pretrained data manifold.

entry.title: Discrete Diffusion Inference-Time Control with Nested Sequential Monte Carlo
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce nested sequential Monte Carlo (NSMC) and fully-adapted NSMC (FA-NSMC) for discrete diffusion language models, improving inference-time reward steering by correcting biases found in earlier formulations.

Why it matters: These methods enable more precise, unbiased control over text generation properties in discrete diffusion models without requiring costly model retraining.

entry.title: The Asymmetric Harms of LLM Compression
entry.summary:
A systematic evaluation of 3 LLMs across 11 compression methods reveals that compression causes asymmetric harms, including disproportionate head knowledge loss, overconfidence in newly lost knowledge, and hidden demographic bias shifts.

Why it matters: Standard aggregate metrics like accuracy and perplexity fail to capture safety risks, overconfidence, and localized performance degradation in compressed LLMs prior to deployment.

entry.title: ReCache: Efficient KV Cache Reuse and Compression for Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
entry.summary:
ReCache enables efficient KV cache reuse and compression for tool-augmented LLM agents through composition-invariant encoding, routing, and pruning.

Why it matters: It allows LLM agents to reuse pre-encoded tool schemas across varying context orders, drastically dropping memory and latency overhead with almost no loss in tool-use accuracy.

entry.title: PEA-DPO: Perception-Enhanced Alignment Direct Preference Optimization for MLLMs Alignment
entry.summary:
PEA-DPO introduces explicit visual preference signals to Direct Preference Optimization to fix visual insensitivity and reduce hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models.

Why it matters: It improves multimodal alignment and substantially reduces visual hallucinations in MLLMs without degrading standard language performance.

entry.title: Pandora's AI Model Routing Box: Efficient Allocation with Costly Value Estimation
entry.summary:
This paper formalizes AI model routing as Pandora's Box, a classical optimal search problem with costly inspection, to balance value estimation accuracy against computational expense.

Why it matters: It enables heterogeneous AI systems to achieve peak routing quality while significantly cutting the computational costs associated with high-accuracy query evaluation.

entry.title: MidTool: Mid-training Data Synthesis for Agentic Tool Use
entry.summary:
MidTool is an open corpus construction pipeline that introduces dedicated mid-training data synthesis from real-world APIs, MCP skills, and document workflows to improve general LLM agentic tool use.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that general agentic tool-use capabilities are more effectively developed during the mid-training phase rather than relying solely on post-training (SFT/RL).

entry.title: Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null
entry.summary:
A study shows language model self-improvement metrics often report false gains caused by measurement artifacts unless evaluated against a separately measured null control from baseline replicates.

Why it matters: Transition-level self-improvement claims require a measured null baseline generated from existing study replicates to prevent mistaking evaluation artifacts for true capability gains.

entry.title: Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization
entry.summary:
Inject, Align, and Recover (IAR) is a three-stage post-training framework that internalizes fixed document corpora into parametric model knowledge for retrieval-free question answering while preserving general capabilities.

Why it matters: IAR enables language models to accurately answer domain-specific questions without requiring a retrieval pipeline at inference time, avoiding the general capability degradation typical of standard fine-tuning.

entry.title: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
entry.summary:
EnvHarness and EnvRigger introduce a programmable layer and automated synthesis system that dynamically wraps static LLM agent environments to target policy weaknesses without altering underlying logic or verifiers.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need to manually build domain-specific environment pipelines, allowing existing agent environments to automatically adapt and scale training to specific policy weaknesses.

entry.title: FACET: Preserving Source Intent and Executable State in Terminal Task Synthesis
entry.summary:
FACET is a framework that synthesizes complex terminal agent tasks by preserving original source intent and using a shared, repaired container state to ensure consistency across instructions, solutions, and verifiers.

Why it matters: It enables the scalable, data-efficient synthesis of complex, validated terminal tasks needed to train and evaluate command-line agents reliably.

entry.title: 4DAnyone: Create Anyone in 4D from a Casual Monocular Video
entry.summary:
4DAnyone reconstructs 4D humans from monocular video by using 4D Gaussian Splatting combined with a video diffusion model that scales to tens of consistent novel views.

Why it matters: It overcomes context-length limits in video diffusion models, enabling high-fidelity 4D human reconstruction and novel-view rendering from casual, uncalibrated single-camera videos.

entry.title: WithEveryone: Unified Planning and Identity Grounding for Group Image Generation
entry.summary:
WithEveryone is a unified framework that scales group image generation up to ten reference identities by injecting identity-addressed tokens and applying Layout-Grounded ID Loss with ID Representation Forcing.

Why it matters: It enables accurate, multi-person image generation for large groups without suffering from duplicate faces, missed identities, or reference copy-paste artifacts.

entry.title: MemTrapBench: Benchmarking Cognitive Traps in LLM Memory Use
entry.summary:
MemTrapBench is a benchmark designed to evaluate memory-induced cognitive traps in LLMs, revealing that faithfully retrieved memories can degrade model reasoning and performance.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that standard long-term LLM memory retrieval can actively impair reasoning and task performance, highlighting the need for defensive inference strategies like AdaptiveMem.

entry.title: SWE-bench Science: Can Coding Agents Resolve Engineering Tasks in Science?
entry.summary:
SWE-bench Science is a new repository-level benchmark containing 119 tasks across 98 GitHub repositories to evaluate coding agents on scientific software engineering.

Why it matters: It establishes a concrete evaluation benchmark exposing how current AI coding agents fail when modifying complex scientific codebases where software errors risk invalidating scientific results.

entry.title: FM-Bench: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Management with Competing Agents
entry.summary:
FM-Bench evaluates LLM agents over a 20-year horizon using 26 tools and up to 400 decision stops to manage a football club against deterministic engines and competing agents in a shared Arena without human judges.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that long-horizon agent performance depends on strategic operational behaviors rather than compute scale, while highlighting critical failure modes in LLM memory management and market inference.

entry.title: ForgeWM: Progressive Causal Training for Few-Step Action-Conditioned Video World Models
entry.summary:
ForgeWM is a four-stage progressive training framework that converts bidirectional action-conditioned video generators into efficient 1-, 2-, and 4-step causal world models for game control.

Why it matters: It enables real-time, low-latency interactive video generation driven by fast-paced user controls without sacrificing visual quality or control alignment.

entry.title: SkillForge: Self-Distilling Agents for Project-Specific Issue Resolution
entry.summary:
SkillForge is a self-distillation framework that proactively acquires project-specific knowledge by synthesizing and solving synthetic issues generated from test-covered repository code.

Why it matters: Proactively extracting and grounding codebase knowledge before encountering real issues enables LLM agents to resolve repository-specific bugs more accurately and efficiently.

entry.title: VA-Judger: Reward Modeling from Human Preference Feedback for Joint Video-Audio Generation
entry.summary:
VA-Judger is a chain-of-thought omni-reward model that uses dimension-wise reinforcement learning on human preference data to improve joint video-audio generation quality.

Why it matters: It provides a human-aligned reward signal for post-training joint video-audio models, preventing reward hacking and improving overall semantic and temporal coherence.

entry.title: Repo0: Design-Driven Zero-to-All Code Generation
entry.summary:
Repo0 is a continuous structural evolution framework for zero-to-all code generation that constructs software projects from natural-language requirements using a Dual-Directed-Acyclic-Graph (Dual-DAG) architectural state.

Why it matters: It enables LLM agents to generate complete, modular software repositories from scratch without needing a predefined architecture.

entry.title: FlashPrefill V2: Block-Sparse Prefill Attention for Long-Context LLM Serving
entry.summary:
FlashPrefill V2 upgrades block-sparse prefill attention into a production-ready engine using mean error correction, optimized FP8 GPU kernels, and native paged KV cache integration.

Why it matters: It transforms theoretical block-sparse prefill optimizations into a deployable backend that drastically speeds up 128K long-context LLM serving in production frameworks.

entry.title: Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization
entry.summary:
The IAR framework improves retrieval-free document knowledge internalization by staging post-training into structured document knowledge injection, answer-only QA alignment, and general capability recovery via model merging.

Why it matters: It enables large language models to accurately answer domain-specific questions without retrieval augmentation while preserving general instruction-following and reasoning abilities.

entry.title: SkillGate: Training In-Policy Skill Selection in Long-Horizon Agents
entry.summary:
SkillGate resolves selector credit starvation in long-horizon agents by splitting credit into distinct outcome-reward channels for execution and local advantage channels for skill selection.

Why it matters: It enables long-horizon agents to accurately select required skills from large libraries without being degraded by noisy sequence-level reinforcement learning rewards.

entry.title: The Problem Is the Problem: Towards Scalable Mathematical Discovery
entry.summary:
The Find, Attempt, and Recommend (FAR) framework automates problem discovery and filtering from literature, reducing human bottlenecks in AI-assisted mathematical research.

Why it matters: It optimizes scarce expert review time and model reasoning resources by automating the search and pre-filtering of mathematical open problems.

entry.title: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement
entry.summary:
AI4AI-Bench introduces 10 frozen research repositories to evaluate LLM agents on rewriting training algorithms for recursive self-improvement, where top systems close less than a fifth of the gap to task optima.

Why it matters: The benchmark isolates an agent's capability to improve core learning algorithms rather than just tuning hyperparameters, offering an empirical measure of progress toward recursive self-improvement.

entry.title: Learning When to Think: Adaptive Reasoning for Test-Time Compute Allocation
entry.summary:
A novel method enables reasoning language models to adaptively select their reasoning depth via a initial token choice, reducing inference token usage while maintaining accuracy.

Why it matters: This approach significantly lowers test-time compute costs and latency by dynamically scaling reasoning effort based on problem difficulty without needing an external routing model.

entry.title: Let's Scale Step by Step: Compute-Efficient Hyperparameter Transfer for Large-Scale Mixture-of-Experts
entry.summary:
A two-step hyperparameter transfer framework uses Maximal Update Parameterization (μP) and scaling laws to accurately predict optimal learning rates for large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models across both model widths and token counts.

Why it matters: It enables accurate tuning of optimal learning rates for massive MoE models using small proxy models, drastically reducing the computational cost of hyperparameter sweeps.

entry.title: EchoCoT: Extracting Hidden Chain-of-Thought from Large Reasoning Models
entry.summary:
EchoCoT is a new multi-step attack framework that extracts near-verbatim hidden chain-of-thought traces from black-box large reasoning models via API tool-call interactions.

Why it matters: It establishes hidden chain-of-thought extraction as a practical security and intellectual property risk for proprietary black-box reasoning models.

entry.title: Inadvertent Context Leakage in Language Models
entry.summary:
In-context secrets implicitly leak into benign language model outputs, enabling an adaptive black-box attack to reconstruct sensitive data even when direct extraction is refused.

Why it matters: AI agents handling sensitive user data risk exposing confidential context through routine, benign responses even when explicit safety guardrails prevent direct extraction.

entry.title: Learning how to Forget: Fine-tuning for Long-Context Sparse Attention
entry.summary:
A new fine-tuning method allows transformer models to co-adapt with any sparse attention KV cache policy using moderate hardware, outperforming models trained with exact attention.

Why it matters: It enables cost-effective fine-tuning and improved long-context inference performance without requiring massive GPU clusters for sequence parallelism.

entry.title: LoRA-GA$^2$: Low Rank Adaptation with Multi-step Gradient Adaptive Alignment
entry.summary:
LoRA-GA$^2$ improves low-rank adaptation by using multi-step gradient information from pretrained weights alongside spectrum-aware rank allocation and optimal initialization.

Why it matters: It narrows the performance gap between LoRA and full fine-tuning without increasing memory overhead.

entry.title: Credit Without Ground Truth: Auditing Step-Level Credit Assignment in LLM Agents Against Executed Replay
entry.summary:
A study auditing LLM agent step-level credit signals against causal ground-truth from executed replays in ALFWorld shows that common credit rules perform no better than chance and primarily echo policy fluency rather than causal step contribution.

Why it matters: Reinforcement learning and fine-tuning methods for LLM agents currently rely on step-level credit signals that fail to reflect actual causal impact, meaning training efficiency is dictated by sample volume rather than true credit assignment.

entry.title: FlashPrefill V2: Block-Sparse Prefill Attention for Long-Context LLM Serving
entry.summary:
FlashPrefill V2 upgrades block-sparse prefill attention for production LLM serving by adding a mean correction term for low FP8/BF16 approximation error and optimizing memory access for engines like SGLang.

Why it matters: It bridges the gap between theoretical sparse attention research and production LLM serving by drastically reducing long-context prefill latency in modern inference frameworks.

entry.title: Truncate Bad, Upweight Good: BoN-Style Distillation via Rank-Based Classification
entry.summary:
TUP is a Best-of-N distillation method that truncates low-ranked candidate completions from the target support and reweights the retained upper tail using a tunable sharpness parameter.

Why it matters: It enables efficient offline policy distillation from Best-of-N sampling without relying on brittle top-rank reward model distinctions or retaining low-quality completions in the target support.

entry.title: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work-Until They Don't
entry.summary:
A contrastive study analyzes LLM agent skills to reveal they primarily act as procedural execution anchors rather than knowledge injectors, while identifying retrieval bottlenecks and failure modes.

Why it matters: Understanding that skills act as procedural anchors rather than fact injectors guides the design of better retrieval mechanisms and more robust self-evolving LLM agents.

entry.title: Zetta ζ: An Efficient Closed-Loop Embodied Harness for Self-Evolving Physical Intelligence
entry.summary:
Zetta is a closed-loop embodied harness that evolves code-based runtime critics and recovery skills online over three timescale-separated loops while keeping the base policy frozen.

Why it matters: It establishes an efficient scaling path for reliable physical intelligence by enabling real-time execution governance and self-evolving recovery skills without expensive policy retraining.

entry.title: Co-RL: Unsupervised Reasoning Emerges from Diverse Cohort in Multi-agent RL
entry.summary:
Co-RL enables unsupervised reasoning in LLMs and VLMs through multi-agent reinforcement learning using peer-derived rewards from a diverse model cohort.

Why it matters: It eliminates the reliance on costly, hard-to-scale ground-truth reward annotations for training advanced reasoning models across text and multimodal domains.

entry.title: SemComp-Bench: Benchmarking Semantic Task Completion in Video Generation
entry.summary:
SemComp-Bench introduces an outcome-oriented benchmark and VLM-based evaluation protocol for video generation, focusing on semantic task completion and grounding rather than intermediate steps or appearance consistency.

Why it matters: It shifts video generation evaluation from strict appearance consistency and full sequence tracking toward functional, goal-oriented task completion.

entry.title: SemaPLC: A Project-Grounded, Verification-Gated Agent Harness for PLC Code Generation
entry.summary:
SemaPLC is an open-source, verification-gated agent harness for PLC code generation that enforces task completion using external compilation, specification, and live runtime trace execution checks.

Why it matters: It establishes live runtime execution and trace comparison, rather than static analysis, as the necessary standard for validating generated industrial control logic.

entry.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
entry.summary:
SPADE is a self-play RL framework where a single LLM acts as an Environment Designer generating executable OpenAI Gym-style environments and a Reasoning Agent that learns to solve them.

Why it matters: Making the environment generator a learnable component solves the goal-stagnation problem in RL, enabling open-ended self-improvement for autonomous language agents.

entry.title: EDITBRIDGE: Towards Faithful and Efficient Ultra-High-Resolution Image Editing
entry.summary:
EditBridge enables faithful ultra-high-resolution (up to 4K) image editing by framing refinement as structured data-to-data translation conditioned on the original high-resolution source using block-wise sparse attention.

Why it matters: It eliminates the quadratic memory constraints of high-resolution diffusion models, enabling fast, artifact-free 4K image editing in professional workflows.

entry.title: DiSCO: Defending text-to-image generation through distribution-guided contrastive prompt optimization
entry.summary:
DiSCO is a zero-shot, black-box defense that uses distribution-guided suffix expansion and contrastive scoring to optimize prompts, preventing NSFW content generation without modifying model weights.

Why it matters: It provides an architecture-agnostic, zero-shot safety defense that can be deployed directly in front of proprietary, black-box text-to-image models without altering their underlying code or weights.

entry.title: LEGO-RL: Harness-Native Reinforcement Learning for Coding Agents
entry.summary:
LEGO-RL bridges long-running native coding-agent harnesses with policy-gradient training using in-process LLM proxying and isolated sandbox orchestration without modifying internal harness control flows.

Why it matters: It enables reliable, scalable reinforcement learning for LLM coding agents directly within off-the-shelf agent execution harnesses without corrupting training signals.

entry.title: Training Leaves Traces: Centered Residual Signatures for Language Model Lineage Verification
entry.summary:
A data-free, white-box lineage verification method uses centered residual signatures from weight matrices to accurately identify open-weight language model ancestry across multiple model families.

Why it matters: It enables passive, fast, and reliable auditability of open-weight LLMs to verify model provenance and detect unauthorized re-skinning or laundering without requiring dataset access.

entry.title: Training Chemical Plausibility-Aware Large Language Models for Single-Step Retrosynthesis
entry.summary:
Researchers trained C3LM using Top-K prompting on a 45.6M reaction dataset and fine-tuned it with ChemCensor-based and novelty rewards for retrosynthesis.

Why it matters: Plausibility-aware Top-K training enables LLMs to generate more diverse and valid reaction pathways, advancing computer-aided synthesis planning.

entry.title: MoE-ViE: Mixture of Experts Vision Encoder for Efficient Image and Video Understanding
entry.summary:
MoE-ViE applies fine-grained Mixture-of-Experts, auxiliary-loss-free balancing, custom inference kernels, and frame-level distillation to scale CLIP-style vision encoders efficiently for image and video understanding.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that MoE vision encoders can achieve state-of-the-art vision-language multimodal performance while significantly reducing compute costs and inference latency compared to dense architectures.

entry.title: Looped Language Models Improve Compositional Tool Calling
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated looped language models on compositional tool calling, finding that recurrent computation at inference time significantly improves multi-step tool coordination, state maintenance, and dependency resolution.

Why it matters: Looped architectures allow agentic AI systems to execute complex multi-step tool workflows more reliably by dynamically allocating compute during inference without increasing parameter count.

entry.title: Decision-Metric Alignment in Latent World Models: Diagnostics and Action-Conditioned Objectives for MPC Planning
entry.summary:
This paper introduces diagnostics and an action-conditioned objective, DA-LeWM, to fix decision-metric misalignment where latent distance fails to correctly rank action sequences in MPC planning.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that strong latent decoding performance is insufficient for planning, proving that explicitly optimizing latent geometry for decision alignment significantly improves online MPC success.

entry.title: SoftVTBench: A Deformation-Aware Visuo-Tactile Dataset and Benchmark for Deformable-Object Manipulation
entry.summary:
SoftVTBench introduces a dataset of 4,000 expert visuo-tactile demonstrations with FEM ground-truth and a benchmark evaluating deformable-object manipulation via a novel Deformation-aware Success Rate (DSR).

Why it matters: It establishes that standard task-completion metrics overlook physical damage during manipulation, providing a standardized framework to develop safer multimodal policies.

entry.title: Harness Continual Learning: Continual Adaptation Beyond Model Parameters
entry.summary:
Harness Continual Learning (HCL) introduces a framework for evolving a frozen foundation model's external harness—including prompts, memories, tools, and routers—while mitigating harness-level catastrophic forgetting.

Why it matters: HCL enables persistent agent improvement and failure recovery through external prompt and memory updates without expensive model fine-tuning or parameter degradation.

entry.title: Test-Time Scaling in the Wild: Why Exploitation, Not Exploration, Is the Bottleneck
entry.summary:
A compute-normalized comparison across five open-ended domains reveals that test-time scaling fails due to poor candidate exploitation rather than insufficient exploration.

Why it matters: Increasing inference compute via current test-time scaling methods yields diminishing returns in open-ended domains unless reward models and candidate selection mechanisms are substantially improved.

entry.title: Training-Free Inference-Time Self-Reflection and Cost-Bounded Early Stopping for Large Language Models
entry.summary:
EvoResearcher is a training-free inference protocol that implements cost-bounded self-reflection and early stopping on a frozen LLM backbone without gradient updates.

Why it matters: It enables LLMs to self-verify and optimize compute budgets at inference time without requiring costly reinforcement learning pipelines like GRPO.

entry.title: Learned, Then Lost: A Measured Single-Example Counterfactual in Pre-training
entry.summary:
Researchers measured the exact counterfactual impact of a single 194-token training injection across 32 124M-parameter GPT-2 models, finding the memory rapidly decays and leaves no detectable final trace on loss barriers or CKA.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that single-example pre-training memory rapidly decays without altering final loss basins provides empirical grounding for counterfactual data attribution and privacy limits in large language models.

entry.title: Gradient Mirage: Trainable yet Label-Unidentifiable Gradients in Large Language Model Split Learning
entry.summary:
Gradient Mirage defends LLM split learning against gradient matching attacks by disrupting gradient-objective consistency while preserving model utility.

Why it matters: It enables secure split learning of large language models by preventing malicious servers from recovering private training labels from shared interface gradients.

entry.title: WhiteMatter: All-to-All Cross-Layer Connections via KV Mixing
entry.summary:
WhiteMatter introduces all-to-all cross-layer connections that route and mix a token's L layer states into k KV-cache channels for subsequent consumer layers to attend to.

Why it matters: It improves Transformer parameter efficiency and performance while significantly reducing KV-cache memory overhead during decoding.

entry.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
entry.summary:
SPADE is a self-play RL framework where a single LLM acts as both an Environment Designer generating executable code environments and a Reasoning Agent learning to solve them.

Why it matters: By making environment synthesis learnable and adaptive rather than static, SPADE enables continuous open-ended self-improvement for language models across complex reasoning and tool-use tasks.

entry.title: Beyond Teacher Likelihood: Group-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning
entry.summary:
Group-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation (GC-OPD) resolves teacher-verifier misalignment in long-context reasoning by combining group-normalized trajectory residuals with token-level Relative-Advantage-Based Credit Assignment (RACA).

Why it matters: It enables long-context language models to retain dense token-level training guidance from teacher models while ensuring alignment with global, response-level task verifiers.

entry.title: Beyond the Transcript: Detecting Covert Co ordination in Latent Multi-Agent Communication
entry.summary:
Verifiable Latent Alignments (VLA) is a framework that monitors and mitigates covert language-model multi-agent communication in continuous hidden states using an activation-aware, neutral-only three-layer monitor and matched counterfactual steering.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that covert, non-transcript multi-agent collusion via continuous hidden states can be effectively detected and steered back to neutral behavior without prior training on attack patterns.

entry.title: Open-MOPD: Diagnosing and Fixing Capability Imbalance in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Open-MOPD diagnoses capability integration failures in multi-teacher on-policy distillation and introduces three budget-rebalancing mechanisms, improving headroom recovery from 35.6% to 83.4% on SmolLM3-3B-Base.

Why it matters: It enables the effective consolidation of multiple domain-specialized RL expert models into a single generalist student without suffering severe cross-domain performance degradation.
